title: How Much Does Herringbone or Chevron Hardwood Flooring Cost to Install?
meta: Herringbone or chevron costs more than plank: $3.25 per sq ft straight-lay labor at Wills Flooring, a pattern premium and 15–20% more material. Lynnwood math.
keywords: herringbone hardwood flooring cost, chevron wood floor installation cost, herringbone vs chevron flooring, herringbone floor labor cost per square foot, parquet pattern hardwood installation, hardwood flooring Lynnwood WA
offers: Hardwood floor installation, engineered or solid

blocks.lead: Straight-lay hardwood installs for $3.25 per sq ft in labor at Wills Flooring; herringbone and chevron start from that rate and add a pattern premium that we quote at the free estimate, plus 15 to 20 percent more material for waste and a pattern-specific product that costs more per box.
blocks.detail: The pattern roughly doubles the number of cuts and the layout time, and chevron is more demanding than herringbone. For a 600 sq ft Lynnwood entry and living room, expect the material order and the labor line to both be noticeably higher than a plank floor of the same size.

blocks.html: Herringbone has gone from a Pinterest board to a real request in Lynnwood, partly because of the new townhomes around the light rail station and partly because owners of 1960s and 70s Alderwood and Martha Lake ramblers are opening up kitchens and want the main floor to look like more than builder plank. The catch: no published price list, including ours, has a single herringbone number, because the pattern cost depends on the room shape, the borders and the product. Here is what drives the premium, the straight-lay math you can count on, and where herringbone is worth it.

blocks.text: Herringbone vs chevron: what you are actually buying

a.title: Rectangular blocks, staggered zigzag
items: Each piece is a normal rectangle with square ends
Pieces meet at 90 degrees, end to side, in a stepped pattern
Uses standard-width engineered or solid planks cut to length, or purpose-made herringbone blocks

b.title: Angled ends meeting in a clean point
items: Each piece is cut at 45 or 60 degrees at both ends and comes in left and right versions
Pieces meet point to point in continuous V lines
Must be purchased as a chevron product; you cannot make it from plank on site without heavy waste

items.title: Layout time
items.text: A plank floor starts from one straight wall. A pattern starts from a center line snapped through the room, squared to the main sight line, with the first rows built on a temporary straightedge. Half a day of layout before a single piece is glued or nailed is normal.

items.title: Cuts at every wall
items.text: On a plank floor, only the ends of each row are cut. In herringbone every piece that touches a wall is cut at an angle, on all four walls. That is the main reason labor runs well above the $3.25 straight-lay rate.

items.title: Flatter subfloor required
items.text: Pattern floors telegraph subfloor dips at every joint because the pieces are short. We often add a leveling step in 1960s ramblers that would be optional under long planks. Subfloor prep is quoted at the estimate.

items.title: Borders and transitions
items.text: A herringbone field usually wants a straight border board around it so the angled cuts do not meet the baseboard raw. Borders add layout and cutting time and look best when planned into the room size.

blocks.text: Where herringbone is worth it, and where it is not

items.html: Worth it: one room you see from the front door. An entry, a dining room or an open living room. The pattern reads immediately and the premium covers a few hundred square feet, not the whole house.
Worth it: a townhome main floor. Lynnwood's new light-rail townhomes have small, square main floors where a pattern makes the room feel finished and larger. Buyers notice it in photos.
Not worth it: bedrooms and hallways. Furniture covers it, and a narrow hall shows only half a pattern. Run plank there in the same product and let the herringbone room be the feature.

Not worth it: a small room with a big pattern. A 10 by 11 ft office in a Martha Lake split-level cannot fit enough repeats to read as herringbone. It reads as a mistake. Scale the block size to the room.
Rethink it: an uneven 1960s subfloor you do not want to level. Short pieces over a wavy floor open at the joints. Either budget for leveling or choose long planks, which bridge dips.

blocks.title: Vinyl plank herringbone is a different product and price:
blocks.text: If you love the look but not the number, herringbone-format vinyl plank exists and installs at the $2.50 per sq ft vinyl rate plus its own pattern premium. It is not hardwood and will not refinish, but for a basement or rental it can make sense. We cover it in our herringbone vinyl plank post.
Questions to ask before you sign a pattern quote

items: Is the pattern premium written as a separate line, so I can compare it to straight plank?
How much material am I ordering over the measured area, and who keeps the leftover?
Where does the pattern center, and did you snap the line to the main sight line from the entry?
Is a border planned, and is it included?
What does the subfloor need, and is leveling in the price?

faq.q: How much more does herringbone cost than regular hardwood flooring?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring, straight-lay hardwood is $3.25 per sq ft in labor. Herringbone starts from that base and adds a pattern premium for the layout and angled cuts, plus 10 to 15 percent more material than plank and a product that often costs more per box. The exact premium depends on the room and is written on your free estimate.

faq.q: Is chevron more expensive than herringbone?
faq.a: Yes, usually on both material and labor. Chevron pieces are pre-cut at an angle in left and right versions, so the product costs more and waste runs 15 to 20 percent. The points have to line up perfectly along every row, which makes the layout slower and less forgiving than herringbone's staggered blocks.

faq.q: Can herringbone be made from regular hardwood planks?
faq.a: Herringbone can. Standard planks cut to a consistent length, typically two to three times their width, make a herringbone field; purpose-made herringbone blocks with matching tongue-and-groove on all sides make it cleaner. Chevron cannot be made from plank on site without wasting a large share of the wood.

faq.q: Does herringbone need a special subfloor?
faq.a: Not a different material, but a flatter one. Short pieces follow every dip in the subfloor, and pattern joints open where long planks would bridge. In many 1960s Lynnwood ramblers we add a leveling step before a pattern floor that we would skip for plank. It is quoted at the estimate after we check the floor.

faq.q: Can herringbone floors be site-finished instead of prefinished?
faq.a: Yes, and unfinished herringbone blocks are a classic choice. Installation is at the unfinished rate of $2.75 per sq ft plus the pattern premium, then the floor is sanded and finished at the refinishing rates, $3.99 natural or $6.50 with stain. The result is a seamless surface with no bevels between pieces.

faq.q: How long does a herringbone installation take?
faq.a: Plan on roughly double the days of a plank floor of the same size. A 600 sq ft herringbone room takes three to four days for prefinished engineered, and chevron four to five. Site-finished adds the sanding and finishing days on top. Stairs, at $125 per stair, are installed as straight treads.
